function.name: list_directory
function.description: List files and subdirectories at a remote path.

skill.skillText: Use `list_directory` to inspect remote file structures before downloading or processing files. Required: `path` (target directory). Example: {path: "/data/reports/2024"}. Verify paths exist, check file names/extensions, or confirm directory contents before further operations. Always validate permissions first.
skill.skillTextSlm: List all files and folders in a specified remote directory using `path` as the target location.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the text content of a remote file.

path.description: Full remote path of the file to read.

maxBytes.description: Maximum bytes to read (default 65536). Use 0 for unlimited.

skill.skillText: Use `read_file` to fetch text from a remote file when you need to process or analyze its content. Required parameter: `path` (file location). Example: read a config file at `/etc/app/config.json` before parsing its settings. Always validate the file exists and is readable.
skill.skillTextSlm: Fetch and return the text content of a file at the specified remote `path`.

function.name: download_file
function.description: Download a remote file. Returns base-64 encoded content and MIME type.

path.description: Full remote path of the file to download.

skill.skillText: Use `download_file` to fetch remote files (e.g., logs, configs) for analysis. Required: `path` (full URL or server path). Returns base64 content and MIME type. Example: Download a log file via `path: /var/log/syslog` or `path: https://example.com/data.csv`. Decode base64 before processing.
skill.skillTextSlm: Download a file from `path`, returning its base-64 content and MIME type for further processing.

function.name: upload_file
function.description: Upload a file to the remote server. Provide either source (local filesystem path) or content (inline UTF-8 text or base64).

path.description: Full remote path where the file should be written.

source.description: Local filesystem path to read and upload (e.g. /Downloads/report.csv). Takes precedence over content when supplied.

content.description: Inline file content – UTF-8 text or base64-encoded bytes.

encoding.description: Set to "base64" when content is base64-encoded (default: utf8).

permissions.description: Optional octal permission string e.g. "755" or "644".

skill.skillText:
Use `upload_file` to transfer files or text to a remote server. Required: `path` (destination). Use `source` for local files or `content` for inline text/base64. Example: upload a config file or script before execution.

Key params: `path`, `source`/`content`. Always verify remote path permissions.
skill.skillTextSlm: Upload a file to the remote server by specifying `path` and providing `source` (local path) or `content` (text/base64).

function.name: make_directory
function.description: Create a directory (and all missing parent directories) on the remote server.

path.description: Full remote path of the directory to create.

skill.skillText: Use `make_directory` when you need to create a directory (including nested parents) on a remote server. Required parameter: `path` (full directory path). Example usage: { "path": "/remote/folder/subfolder" }. Ideal for setup tasks before file operations.
skill.skillTextSlm: Create a directory and any missing parents on the remote server using `make_directory` with the required `path` parameter.

function.name: remove_directory
function.description: Remove an EMPTY directory on the remote server. Fails if the directory is not empty.

path.description: Full remote path of the empty directory to remove.

skill.skillText: Use `remove_directory` to delete an empty directory on a remote server. Required param: `path` (full directory path). Fails if directory contains files. Example: remove_directory /home/user/empty_folder. Verify directory is empty before use to avoid errors.
skill.skillTextSlm: Delete an empty remote directory at *path*; fails if non-empty or inaccessible.

function.name: list_scripts
function.description: List all saved shell scripts in the local script library.

skill.skillText:
Use `list_scripts` to quickly audit or locate saved scripts in your MCP library before execution or editing.
Key parameters: `--filter <keyword>` (optional, narrows results).
Example: `list_scripts --filter backup` to find backup-related scripts. Outputs names and paths.
skill.skillTextSlm: Use `list_scripts` to display all saved shell scripts in your local MCP script library for quick access.

function.name: run_script
function.description: Run a saved script from the local script library by name. ALWAYS use this (never execute_command) when the user says "call script NAME", "run script NAME", or provides a script name with arguments. Numbers after the script name are script arguments — put them in args.

scriptName.description: The name of the saved script to run.

scriptId.description: Optional id of the saved script (overrides scriptName).

args.description: Arguments passed to the script as a space-separated string (e.g. "15" or "/tmp 6"). These are the script's own parameters, not a timeout.

skill.skillText: Use `run_script` when the user explicitly names a script to execute (e.g., *run script backup* or *call script cleanup 5*). Required: `scriptName` (exact name). Optional: `args` for numeric/script inputs (e.g., *script delay 30* → `args: [30]`). Never use `execute_command` for scripts. Example: `run_script(scriptName: "restart_service", args: [10])`.
skill.skillTextSlm: Use `run_script` to execute a local script by name when requested, passing trailing numbers as `args` (e.g., *run script backup 30*). Never use `execute_command` for scripts.

function.name: execute_command
function.description: Execute a raw ad-hoc shell command. Use ONLY for one-off commands like "df -h" or "systemctl status nginx". Do NOT use this to run a script from the script library — use run_script for that.

skill.skillText:
Use `execute_command` for quick, one-off shell commands (e.g., `df -h`, `systemctl status nginx`). Avoid scripts—use `run_script` instead.
**Key param**: `command` (string, required).
Example: `execute_command command="ls -la /tmp"` for directory listing. Always validate output.
skill.skillTextSlm: Run a single shell command like `df -h` via `execute_command`; avoid scripts—use `run_script` instead. Key param: `command`.
